entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider. It supports memory at the user, session, and agent levels, and is available as an OSS SDK, a self-hosted server, or managed cloud.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides agent memory designed to learn over time through retain, recall, and reflect operations. Its reported state-of-the-art LongMemEval benchmark performance distinguishes it as a benchmark-focused option.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that stores context in a viking:// virtual filesystem. Its tiered L0/L1/L2 loading uses generated summaries, and the project reports evaluations on LoCoMo and tau2-bench.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee turns documents, code, and conversations into a searchable knowledge graph for persistent agent memory across sessions. It can run locally without an API key using small CPU models.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, as well as an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts facts from conversations and handles contradictions. Its single API covers memory, RAG, and connectors, with plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and others.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes agents that stores explicit facts with sources and supports corrections and withdrawal. It starts with keyless memory and keyword retrieval, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and is the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It stores messages and events on sessions and reasons in the background to update peer representations; deployment options include managed, local CLI, and self-hosted FastAPI server.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, with brv vc commit, branch, and merge operations for a plain Markdown context tree. Its five-tier retrieval includes four non-LLM tiers, and the project also offers a React/Ink TUI and REPL.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto manages agent memory through extract, consolidate, reconcile, forget, and brief operations. It connects to tools including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Cline, Goose, and Copilot, and can export a memory estate as Open Knowledge Format Markdown.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that combines vector search, structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. Its local infrastructure uses Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, while a Ground Truth hierarchy guides the agent to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents tackle complex tasks by generating playbooks, datasets, and local-model training artifacts from task runs. It offers CLI, MCP server, and Pi extension entry points, and supports Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, vLLM, and Ollama endpoints.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: A Hermes Agent plugin that persists messages in a SQLite-backed hierarchical DAG, with recall tools such as lcm_grep and lcm_recall for recovering details. Its focus on retaining and retrieving message history makes it a fit for agents that need lossless context management.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches local session history across supported coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, and OpenClaw. It can surface relevant past sessions at startup or after command failures, using a local index without a model, embeddings, or server.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho memory backend for private, cross-session persistence in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, and includes an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: SignetAI provides a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer with portable state across several agents and MCP clients. It can create memories from transcripts and imported files, while its Dreaming feature builds a cited knowledge graph of people and projects.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk, offering an inspectable format for multi-agent systems. It provides local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback; its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine with a local SQLite vault shared across Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes. Its retrieval combines BM25 and vector search with rank fusion and reranking, and it can import conversation exports from several sources.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory is a file-based long-term memory system offered as a five-package family, including an SDK, CLI, MCP server, Hermes adapter, and LangGraph BaseStore. Its SQLite-backed, five-tier schema uses FTS5 search without a vector database or embedding model.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes long-context inference through context reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling. It supports text and multimodal reordering for prefix-cache sharing and integrates with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin provides explainable retrieval, attaching a why_retrieved tag to each recall result and supporting canonicalization, contradiction tracking, and recency ranking. Its default backend runs in-process, and its self-directing gap-to-task loop is enabled by default.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn keeps durable, cross-project memory in inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven memory CLI maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history, so knowledge can persist and evolve across sessions. It supports proactive recall and maintenance without requiring embeddings or a vector database.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-QMD uses an anticipatory cache that watches agent session logs to prefetch context, combining RAG and vector search. It stores data locally with SQLite-vec and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner for Hermes. It uses SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval, and supplies the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep provides reflective memory with semantic search, BM25 full-text search, and ranked graph traversal. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags link notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens through local keyword-based ranking and supports Tool Search. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19+, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides Git-backed context and workflows in plain Markdown for Claude Code, Codex, and compatible coding agents. It includes adapters for multiple agents and reviewed handoffs with hash-checked proposals and receipts.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes memory plugin stores data in a single embedded .lbdb graph database file. Its importance-weighted recall surfaces higher-priority memories during context prefetch, alongside BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships between entries.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes local capabilities and routes queries to whole artifacts rather than chunks. It registers five tools in the local_knowledge toolset and enables implicit feedback by default.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and support for immediate event deletion. It also records prefetch operations in a trace.jsonl audit log.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail offers a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: Hermes XMemo provides durable cross-session memory through native pre-turn recall and session-end snapshots. It uses a local SQLite layer for caching and write-outbox reliability, and can read memories from other connected agents.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: This Hermes plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, including semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands include /code-search and /code-ask with citations; it requires a separately installed backend, and requests are HMAC-signed and sent over localhost only.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest by default and native Rust FFI or HTTP daemon execution modes. Its retrieval options include HNSW ANN, sparse search, and FM-index retrieval.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides 17 tools for memory management and knowledge graph traversal in Hermes. It combines BM25, vector, and graph methods for hybrid search, and can checkpoint context automatically during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit is a file-based memory curation loop: it takes Markdown and outputs JSON diffs for review, without a database. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert memory changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides composable skills with instructions designed to make agents use them, alongside a software-development workflow covering specification, design sign-off, planning, and subagent execution. It belongs in this list for teams seeking a defined development methodology; installation is handled separately for each harness, with multiple harnesses documented.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first design and prototyping system that can generate web prototypes, slides, images, and motion graphics. It supports coding-agent integrations including Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot, and provides native runtime support for the DeepSeek Harness agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project offers a structured cybersecurity skill collection spanning 34 security domains, with skills mapped to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. Its stated compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms makes it a broad option for adding security-focused skills to agents.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language descriptions and real sources into editable .drawio files. Its incremental sync is designed to preserve manual layout and annotations, and it also offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills for agent-to-agent commerce, with natural-language mandates, delegated permissions, payments, and escrow among its stated capabilities. It also includes vendored copies of official protocol skills and a verification and dispute-resolution layer.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing audits and rewrites content to address detectable AI writing patterns, with modes for rewriting, detection, and editing in place. Optional voice profiles and detector access through the CLI, GitHub Actions, pre-commit, or MCP make it useful across different writing workflows.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to automate skill deduplication and quality improvement, while unifying skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members. It integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code and agents that support agentskills.io. It also supports Codex and agent-plugins.org specifications, and maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection provides 822 professional agent skills as plain Markdown SKILL.md files, including skills that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code. An installer copies selected skills into tool configuration folders, and the package also includes an MCP server and read-only REST API.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube Skills gives agents tools for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It supports Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills, then generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-Hermes teaches Hermes Agent to generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks, with pre-built analytical lenses for different domains. It reports findings alongside identified blind spots in the analysis.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, including remote skill registries from Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and script execution, with sandboxing to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design and implementation documents for Hermes Agent, with Lite and Full modes for different project complexities. A spec review gate evaluates documents using PASS/FAIL models before handoff.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that combine prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files with a tangler. It also syncs source-file edits back into the literate document, linking code and documentation across agents.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents, using a mechanism kernel for SQLite storage and event logging. It coordinates agent teams through the SLP cooperative-agent protocol and shares prompt-first working methods as Markdown recipes and skills.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format, alongside guides for installation, configuration, and use. Its contribution process uses forks and pull requests, making it a resource for Portuguese-speaking users and contributors.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation, plus BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills specification, with installation instructions using npx skills add. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agentskills.io-compliant skills from repositories, documentation, or SaaS APIs, generating instruction files with AST-based source-code citations. Provenance maps and evidence reports provide an audit trail for the generated material.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Lets users define repeatable AI work in a .nika file, with a Rust binary to run it. The nika check command audits workflows before any model is called, and each run leaves a hash-chained, verifiable record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, along with a Python client and CLI. Its installation flow resolves dependencies recursively, and the project also includes TON payment features.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Checkpoints and built-in rollback procedures help with recovery during execution.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It belongs on the list for bringing these personal data tools together, with HTTPS App Password authentication and a guided setup script for credential validation and configuration.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: Hermeshub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, with federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face. Its implementation of the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification makes it a discovery-focused addition to the list.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye retrieves relevant Hermes Agent skills using five layers, including hard triggers and semantic embeddings. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage; it also degrades gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, read-only dashboard for monitoring Hermes Agent activity, including token costs, session history, skill analytics, and incidents. Its local-first approach includes log desensitization, with optional incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This skill creates reproducible demo GIFs for repository READMEs, using vhs tape files or Playwright recording scripts. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, and optimizes GIFs toward a target size under 8 MB.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches RemoteOpenClaw’s catalog of MCP servers, agent skills, and plugins, and provides installation commands for discovered tools. It integrates with MCP-compatible clients including Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: Agent Skill Builder generates Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field changes that could leave skills out of date.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: Skill Evolution analyzes session history to identify skill coverage gaps and draft structured improvement proposals. Updates are gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators, and it runs locally with Python’s standard library.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using the path syntax appropriate to native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, or WSL. They also select and verify existing Python interpreters that are compatible with a project.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage provides agent skills for social data, CRM management, and lead enrichment, with support for Claude Code, Cursor, and other agentskills.io-compliant clients. It also includes an MCP server for browser-based OAuth authentication.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes tools to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, remove common Chinese AI-writing patterns, and extract structured data from PDFs and images. Its text de-humanizer uses a rule-based engine, while PDF and image extraction uses macOS Vision.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets users answer support bounties for USDC or create and manage their own funded bounty boards. Its tools support listing bounties, buying context, and submitting drafts, with payments on Base via x402.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: Openclaw Skills automates payments for HTTP 402 responses using USDC and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: SkillSeal tests AI agent skills in isolated Docker containers for structure, functionality, and security. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates that can be verified through its public API.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, exposing 191 tools. It also includes five workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates Chinese news briefings at scales ranging from global to street level. It produces structured reports with conclusions and action suggestions, and uses semantic memory of user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology, with deterministic results and SHA-256 hashes for verification. The endpoint requires no authentication and supports per-call REST payment via x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with incremental discovery of server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a fit for this list of skills focused on efficient MCP access.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system for habits and study blocks, with agent-driven scheduling and system design through an MCP connection. It stands out for pairing that agent control with local storage in a single SQLite file, plus a React web app and an Expo-based Android app.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard runs adversarial code reviews with three parallel subagents focused on edge cases, adversarial review, and integration analysis, then consolidates and triages their findings. It adds deterministic pre-scans and verifies findings with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox; it is read-only and does not fix code.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-multichannel-prompt-opt: This Hermes Agent plugin rewrites and scores prompts across CLI, TUI, Discord, Telegram, and other surfaces. It is retired and archived as read-only; in a test of 100 messages comparing rewritten and original answers, neither version passed the preference condition.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill uses parallel Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness agents to simplify code in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust. Its tiered application process includes an approval gate, making it a code-focused option for teams that want to review changes before they are applied.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts fablize’s verified procedures, breaking tasks into multiple stories with mandatory evidence-based verification gates. It also provides a systematic protocol for reproducing issues and debugging causes, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state management.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: A turnkey cybersecurity lab for Hermes Agent, with CVE-driven skills and tools for network security, forensics, and exploitation. It belongs in this list for its broad coverage of 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including MITRE ATT&CK, MISP, CVSS, EPSS, OWASP, NIST, Sigma, and YARA.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: A C#/.NET implementation of agentskills.io, it uses SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure and integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading. It belongs on this list for bringing that skill-loading approach to .NET, with automatic registration of common agent skill directories.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: A collection of Markdown skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and generic targets, installed by copying a directory into an agent’s skills folder. It covers session management, multi-session reconciliation, worktree recovery, PR review, and skill scaffolding; the project is in maintenance mode, with security fixes only.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project provides daily-updated Nix packages for AI coding agents, including Hermes, across terminal, desktop, and IDE environments. It is included for users seeking a package-managed approach to development tools on Nix-supported systems.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone offers an automated installer and configuration guides for running the Antigravity CLI and OpenClaw on ARM64 Android devices via Termux. It enables mobile deployment by leveraging Termux:API and Termux:GUI for hardware and interface access.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This repository features a Termux-based automated installation script that utilizes proot-distro Ubuntu to run Hermes Agent on Android. It supports interactive model setup, shell command execution, and connectivity with both local Ollama models and external providers.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This community Helm chart facilitates Kubernetes deployments by enforcing single-writer state safety for persistent storage. It supports both direct deployments and operator-ready workflows with configurable gateway, API, and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: Providing a one-command installer for both Android (Termux) and iOS (iSH), this project brings the Hermes AI assistant to mobile platforms. It distinguishes itself by integrating Telegram for voice and file messaging alongside support for scheduled cron jobs.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: Hermesclaw provides a sandboxed environment for Hermes Agent using NVIDIA OpenShell for hardware-enforced security. It implements kernel-level restrictions on network and filesystem access while allowing for configurable security policies regarding web searches and messaging.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying and operating Hermes agents on Docker and Kubernetes via Helm charts. It features a 69-entry credential catalog, support for over 17 LLM providers, and mandatory AES-256-GCM encryption for all secrets.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image that combines the official Hermes installation with mini-swe-agent. It supports persistent state through mounted directories and allows users to target specific Hermes versions using build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module enables reproducible deployments through declarative configuration of workspace documents and settings. It offers a hybrid management system for skills and integrates with sops-nix for secure secrets handling via systemd.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane designed to orchestrate multiple agent instances with distinct identities and workspaces from a single web application. It manages granular permissions for tools and networks while providing dedicated Telegram and WhatsApp communication channels.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: Targeting headless Ubuntu and Debian environments, this project configures the Hermes Gateway as a reboot-safe systemd service. It is designed for production-ready autonomous execution of recurring AI tasks via cron jobs.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable distribution that runs from USB drives without requiring host installation or registry modifications. It bundles Python, PortableGit, and rescue tools to support Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes in offline or isolated environments.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a multi-agent LLM framework for financial trading in which specialized agents such as analysts, traders, and risk managers debate to evaluate market conditions. It belongs in this list as an example of role-specialized agents collaborating through debate, and the README notes it is designed for research rather than financial advice.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted orchestration layer for dispatching tasks, running multi-agent workflows, and monitoring spend. It governs task assignment, agent registration, memory browsing, and cost tracking, and exposes these capabilities through a Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API. It can be installed locally via Node.js or deployed with Docker.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini. It keeps persistent agent sessions running in the background via tmux, supports sandboxing with Docker, Podman, and Apple Containers, and offers dashboards with diff review.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: This project is a Control Room-first template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent into specialist teams and automated workflows. It uses a level-based architecture and a task bus pattern for orchestrator-to-specialist delegation and handoffs, and bundles skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: Swarmclaw is a framework for building autonomous AI agent swarms with orchestration, skills, and support for multiple model providers. It supports 23+ LLM providers including OpenAI and Ollama, provides durable agent memory and MCP tool integration, and includes visual org charts for delegating work across agent teams.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a Mission Control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work from a single screen. It presents a Kanban board for tracking task status and review queues, streams agent reasoning and tool execution live, and requires human-in-the-loop verification for every agent-proposed task completion.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized AI agents covering research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. It follows a strict pipeline architecture and includes a Master Orchestrator responsible for routing and coordination, making it a structured pipeline-based entry in this list.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local multi-agent collaboration web system built on Hermes Agent profiles, MCP, ACP, and Hermes Kanban. It orchestrates Leader and Specialist agents for automated task lifecycle management, integrates MCP and ACP for local tool and communication handling, and provides a real-time Web UI for monitoring agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: This meta-harness for Hermes Agent focuses on meta-optimization, automating outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code. It orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 benchmark evaluations and provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking, distinguishing it as an optimization-oriented rather than task-execution framework.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator stages an agent-vs-agent arena in which autonomous AI companies compete for GitHub stars. It orchestrates 9 autonomous agents across two competing companies, using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, and includes a real-time dashboard visualizing agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a fully local multi-model agent framework that runs a Mixture-of-Agents stack on consumer GPUs with Hermes and Ollama and no cloud dependencies. It implements Mixture-of-Agents through parallel model querying and synthesis, uses Hermes for task routing and tool-calling, and is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph provides a local, pre-indexed code knowledge graph that coding agents can query to reduce token usage and tool calls. It connects to agents through an MCP server and automatically syncs the graph when files change. This makes it a fit for Hermes Agent setups where grounding code understanding in a local index matters.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale is a CLI tool for tracking token usage and costs across AI coding agents, including Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, and Gemini. It reads data from each client's local storage paths and offers a submit command for a leaderboard and public profile. It belongs here as a cross-agent accounting utility for developers watching spend.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for inspecting coding-agent API traffic from Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and OpenCode, among others. It provides a self-contained HTML viewer for exported trace sessions and redacts common authentication headers before recording. This makes it useful for debugging and auditing agent requests without sending traces elsewhere.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, cost, and rate limits that reads Hermes Agent state directly alongside Claude Code, Codex, and other CLIs. It reads local data paths per listed tool and separates token usage, limits, and session details. Multi-device sync and historical usage trends make it a monitoring companion for agent-heavy workflows.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build better UI with AI. It is compatible with any AI provider supporting markdown or general prompting and integrates with Hermes Agent, Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot. It earns a place here as an interface-design aid for agent-assisted development.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It loads 36 skills and 6 workflows directly into Hermes Agent and coordinates seven specialized agent roles through a CTO loop. It also automates deployment, health checks, and log observation across VPS or local environments.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins offers community CLI skins and themes for the Hermes terminal UI. It customizes banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art banners, with YAML-based configuration for creating themes such as retro DOS and cyberpunk aesthetics. It fits this list as a lightweight personalization layer for Hermes users.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang is a static linter for AI agent configs, tool descriptions, and system prompts that uses HERM v1.1 scoring. It performs scans with no model calls or network access, and its findings name the file and propose a specific fix. It emits JSON, SARIF, and GitLab Code Quality reports, making it useful for CI-friendly validation of agent assets.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments. It belongs here as infrastructure for agent interaction and payments rather than a coding tool.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP. It has built-in support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers, plus a supervisor sidebar for managing agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads. It also supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes CCC is a port of the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to the Claude Code Channel. It runs natively in Claude Code without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized into two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin auto-captures and auto-recalls context. It fits this list as a memory integration layer for agent workflows.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: A preconfigured Hermes Agent setup that pairs RTK and Caveman templating to cut token usage by 90-99%, aimed at developers who want lower-cost agent runs out of the box. It ships with 40+ pre-configured skills spanning finance, devops, and research, plus automated cross-platform installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: A TAW Agent framework for building scoped Hermes Agents, where each folder carries its own local configuration and skills. It switches between default and scoped agents and supports project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions, making it useful when one workspace needs different agent behavior than another.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: A setup package that gets a hermes-agent stack running in minutes using free models, 29 plugins, and zero cost. It automates installation of hermes-agent alongside 12+ supporting services and offers three scalable deployment tiers, from a minimum viable setup to a production stack, with plugins organized across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: A migration tool for moving from OpenClaw to Hermes Agent, transferring SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives. It maps OpenClaw configs and credentials into Hermes YAML and JSON formats, sets up systemd gateway services, and handles nested auth structures.
entries.observeco/observeco: Self-healing observability for AI agents that discovers, monitors, and auto-recovers multi-agent systems without a cloud dependency. Its native Hermes plugin exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations, and it offers two monitoring modes—zero-token passive analysis and scheduled active probing—while config-aware baselines detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: A voice-enabled personal assistant for Hermes Agent with an open mic and wake word, running fully local with no API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro, and adds adaptive turn-taking and barge-in for more natural spoken interaction.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: A deterministic, zero-network local runtime by default, intended to help users make their first genuine dollar online with Hermes Agent. It requires explicit approval for all consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer-previews, and exact-approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: A Hermes memory plugin for MemOS that provides semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It includes tools for searching, adding, and deleting memories, along with a circuit breaker to handle MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other coding agents and CLIs. It provides one-click API provider switching and centralized management for MCP, Skills, and Prompts, reducing the need to hand-edit configuration files.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with support for autonomous multi-step tasks that can request user approval and access files. Its built-in assistants generate editable office files, and cron scheduling and remote access interfaces support unattended automation.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides browser-based access to Hermes Agent, including from a phone, in a three-panel layout for sessions, chat, and workspace files. It uses Python and vanilla JavaScript without a build step, framework, or bundler, and runs the agent in-process using HERMES_HOME configuration.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent. It offers a guided first-run install, local or remote backend connections, and a streaming chat interface with 22 slash commands.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a local-first workspace for multi-agent chat and workflows, with session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, and Docker distribution, and provides unified configuration for 10 platform channels.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace brings chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector into a native web workspace. It also offers Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser, Monaco editor, and PTY terminal.
entries.xintaofei/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes and other agents in a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate with @, or queue tasks in separate worktrees; it includes 15 agents and supports ACP agents.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH and presents sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs in dedicated views. An embedded terminal provides direct shell access for system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent that also supports macOS, with native window and process management. Its interface includes chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering, while the built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel provides health checks and updates.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime. It supports local, Cloud, or remote connections, while Bot Mode adds agent switching and group chats; Firefox does not include Chromium-only real-tab attach.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes Agent from a phone, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It is a client-only app for iOS 18 and later; users run the server themselves, and the app is free with no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace shows code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI monitor with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and includes a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: Agent Sessions is a native Mac app for searching 16 local agent histories, including Hermes sessions. It also tracks per-session Codex and Claude quota usage, builds its search index locally, and uses no telemetry.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted browser dashboard brings together a terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel for the Hermes stack. It also offers streaming chat with tool-call visualization, MCP server lifecycle controls, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: Hermes Desktop OS1 is a native macOS workspace for running Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts. It can install Hermes Agent on a fresh cloud computer with one click and includes WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent to a web dashboard through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests that have side effects.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also provides a kanban board for work and task management, plus controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run, mobile-first React SPA provides a 10-page dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its terminal chat supports streaming responses and file attachments, while background agent spawning supports up to five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent is a desktop version for Windows 10 and 11 that requires no installation, Docker, or admin rights. It includes 100 tools across more than 20 toolsets, with TTS, Music, and ComfyUI extensions that auto-install on first use.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a glassmorphic web interface for a self-hosted Hermes Agent, with chat and real-time log streaming. Its dashboard also combines file browsing and task tracking with management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes, showing session activity and cost tracking in real time. It also supports inspecting conversation histories and skill source code, alongside read-only views of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan UI is a self-hosted, chat-first workspace with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. Its marketplace supports discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, while isolated profiles keep sessions, memory, and API keys separate.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client provides streaming chat and model switching for Hermes Agent, with a PM orchestrator coordinating collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents. It also includes a visual Skill Store with more than 50 curated one-click installations.
